chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Reclining in the Masjid is the monasticism of the Arabs. Indeed, the believer's sitting place is his Masjid, and his monastery is his house.'

key_terms.الِاتِّكَاءُ: Reclining or leaning back in a relaxed posture
key_terms.صَوْمَعَتُهُ: His monastery or cell of worship
key_terms.مَجْلِسُهُ: His sitting place or gathering place

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of reclining in the mosque according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the Arab practice of excessive reclining in mosques to pre-Islamic monasticism (Rahbaniyyah), critiquing it as a form of spiritual passivity. He redefines the believer's spiritual geography by asserting that the mosque is the locus of public devotion, while the home becomes the private sanctuary for worship, thereby balancing communal and domestic piety in Shia tradition.
